notes:
Section 2 of RFC 7863 presents the NFSv4.2 protocol definition in the XDR language of RFC 4506, which it cites normatively. Lines that begin with "%" are not part of that language. The "%" prefix is an rpcgen convention: rpcgen copies the rest of the line verbatim into its generated C output. An XDR compiler that implements RFC 4506 rejects these lines. A code generator for another target language, such as Rust or Python, has no use for the C they contain.

Most of the "%" lines in Section 2 carry only comments and can become ordinary XDR comments without changing the protocol. The block quoted above carries C preprocessor directives and a C typedef that import authsys_parms from the host's RPC headers. Without that block, the extracted XDR does not define authsys_parms, which callback_sec_parms4 uses for its AUTH_SYS arm. The extracted XDR does not define AUTH_NONE, AUTH_SYS, or RPCSEC_GSS either, although callback_sec_parms4 and secinfo4 use them as case labels. The corrected text supplies these definitions in XDR, taken from RFC 5531 Section 8.2 and Appendix A.
